llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the saved .docx file from the VM via env.controller.get_file() and uses python-docx to extract run-level font name and size properties.
Metric correctly checks both task requirements: font name equals 'Times New Roman' with all_same_font=True (0.5 pts) and font size approximately 14.0pt with all_same_size=True (0.5 pts).
Expected values in evaluator config match the instruction exactly: expected_font='Times New Roman', expected_size_pt=14.0.
Partial credit design (0.5+0.5) is appropriate for the two composed sub-goals.
Negative control resistance is good: original document uses Georgia 15pt, so both checks fail at initial state.
postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring state is persisted to disk.

Minor concern: getter only captures run.font.name and run.font.size at the run level; runs with style-inherited properties return None and are excluded. However, applying formatting via Ctrl+A + font toolbar in LibreOffice sets explicit run-level properties, so this works correctly for the demonstrated interaction pattern.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also inspecting paragraph-level and document default style font properties (para.style.font) as a fallback when run.font.name/size is None, to handle cases where font is applied through styles rather than direct run formatting.
